Lagos Commuter and Transit Survey - Retrieval-Optimised Knowledge
Base
This document summarises a survey of 333 Lagos commuters. Each section is written so that a single paragraph can be
understood on its own. Currency is the Nigerian Naira, written as NGN (for example NGN 1,200 means 1,200 Naira). Fares are the
amount the commuter paid for one trip. Travel time was collected as bands (Under 30 minutes, 30 to 60 minutes, 1 to 2 hours, Over
2 hours, and for some respondents 2 to 3 hours or Over 3 hours); averages stated in minutes are estimates computed from band
midpoints. Time of day is one of five departure periods: Early Morning Rush (5:00 AM to 7:59 AM), Mid-Morning / Off-Peak (8:00

AM to 11:59 AM), Afternoon / Mid-day (12:00 PM to 3:59 PM), Evening Rush (4:00 PM to 7:59 PM) and Night (8:00 PM to 11:00
PM). Origin LGA and Destination LGA are the Local Government Areas of the starting point and final destination.
Data caveats: the survey is a convenience sample, not a statistical sample of all Lagos commuters. Many routes have only a few
responses, so averages for a single route and time of day can rest on one or two people and should be treated as anecdotal. Fares
were cleaned from free text (symbols such as # and N removed; ranges averaged; unusable answers such as 80p or 1,200 per day
excluded). Where a respondent skipped a question it is stated as not reported.
1. Overall survey summary

1. Overall survey summary
Overall (all 333 responses): 333 survey responses; average fare NGN 1,701, median fare NGN 1,200, lowest NGN 200, highest
NGN 20,000 (based on 329 fare answers); travel time (from 333 answers): most common band is 30 to 60 minutes; breakdown -
Under 30 minutes: 71, 30 to 60 minutes: 114, 1 to 2 hours: 89, Over 2 hours: 36, 2 to 3 hours: 21, Over 3 hours: 2; estimated
average travel time about 1 hour 11 minutes (computed from band midpoints, so approximate).
Evening Rush responses overall: 22 survey responses; average fare NGN 1,325, median fare NGN 1,000, lowest NGN 300,
highest NGN 6,000 (based on 22 fare answers); travel time (from 22 answers): most common band is 30 to 60 minutes; breakdown

- Under 30 minutes: 6, 30 to 60 minutes: 9, 1 to 2 hours: 5, Over 2 hours: 1, 2 to 3 hours: 1; estimated average travel time about 58
minutes (computed from band midpoints, so approximate). Evening rush is the smallest peak period in this survey, so route-level
evening figures are thin.
2. Frequently asked questions answered from the data
Q: What is the average fare and travel time from Ikorodu to Ikeja during evening rush?
A: Only 1 survey respondent travelled from Ikorodu to Ikeja in the Evening Rush (4:00 PM - 7:59 PM). That commuter (Ikorodu to
Alausa, Ikeja, by Korope / Mini-bus (7-Seater)) paid NGN 3,000 and reported travel time of Over 2 hours. So the average fare for

this route in the evening rush is NGN 3,000 and the average travel time is over 2 hours, but this rests on a single response and is
not a reliable average.
Q: What about the opposite direction, Ikeja to Ikorodu in the evening rush?
A: Ikeja LGA to Ikorodu LGA in the Evening Rush: 3 survey responses; average fare NGN 1,233, median fare NGN 1,200, lowest
NGN 1,200, highest NGN 1,300 (based on 3 fare answers); travel time (from 3 answers): most common band is 30 to 60 minutes;
breakdown - 30 to 60 minutes: 3; estimated average travel time about 45 minutes (computed from band midpoints, so
approximate). Origins: Maryland, Maryland, Ikeja.

Lagos Commuter and Transit Survey - Retrieval-Optimised Knowledge
Base
This document summarises a survey of 333 Lagos commuters. Each section is written so that a single paragraph can be
understood on its own. Currency is the Nigerian Naira, written as NGN (for example NGN 1,200 means 1,200 Naira). Fares are the
amount the commuter paid for one trip. Travel time was collected as bands (Under 30 minutes, 30 to 60 minutes, 1 to 2 hours, Over
2 hours, and for some respondents 2 to 3 hours or Over 3 hours); averages stated in minutes are estimates computed from band
midpoints. Time of day is one of five departure periods: Early Morning Rush (5:00 AM to 7:59 AM), Mid-Morning / Off-Peak (8:00

AM to 11:59 AM), Afternoon / Mid-day (12:00 PM to 3:59 PM), Evening Rush (4:00 PM to 7:59 PM) and Night (8:00 PM to 11:00
PM). Origin LGA and Destination LGA are the Local Government Areas of the starting point and final destination.
Data caveats: the survey is a convenience sample, not a statistical sample of all Lagos commuters. Many routes have only a few
responses, so averages for a single route and time of day can rest on one or two people and should be treated as anecdotal. Fares
were cleaned from free text (symbols such as # and N removed; ranges averaged; unusable answers such as 80p or 1,200 per day
excluded). Where a respondent skipped a question it is stated as not reported.
